headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: default write access and broad egress create dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read/write local files and use MCP, and Windsurf exposes clipboard plus workspace files while ECC writes to ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc. That creates a default shared-content bridge where one agent can ingest the other's outputs as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible without unusual setup, though not as severe as raw web-to-agent parsing.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or synced notes directory, injected instructions can cross between them.
IF either agent reads file contents as authoritative prompts, malicious content in shared files can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and config roots for each agent.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Use a read-only export file for inter-agent transfer.
Add a manual review step before one agent consumes the other's output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files and reject untrusted instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, hooks, agent definitions, and security findings, while Windsurf reads workspace files and sends content to its model proxy/MCP. Because both have filesystem access and broad network paths, sensitive material from ECC-managed files can flow into Windsurf's inference backend by default in a shared workspace. The blast radius includes secrets and security findings, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ECC stores secrets or security findings in shared files, Windsurf can ingest them through workspace access.
IF both agents operate under the same user profile, local file leakage can reach Windsurf's remote model proxy.
mitigations: Move sensitive ECC files out of the shared workspace.
Restrict Windsurf to a sanitized project copy.
Rotate any secrets already present in shared files.
Turn off auto-upload or remote model features where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and git-state modification, and Windsurf explicitly shares state via local filesystem. ECC also notes shared-state concerns across instances. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git operations can overwrite each other without locking, making destructive conflicts likely in default use.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or branch, concurrent writes can clobber files or commits.
IF either agent auto-runs git operations, race conditions can corrupt working state.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Use git worktrees or separate clones.
Review diffs before any commit or merge.
requires-engineering: add file locks and transaction-style coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf's Cascade loop can act on generated code, and ECC produces session summaries, skills, and security findings that Windsurf may treat as input. With both agents able to execute shell and modify git state, an error in ECC's output can be propagated and operationalized by Windsurf into commits or commands. That is a default dangerous cascade with potentially irreversible repo changes.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes ECC-generated summaries or findings as authoritative, it can act on incorrect facts.
IF either agent is allowed to auto-execute commands, mistaken outputs can become filesystem or git changes.
mitigations: Require human review of ECC outputs before Windsurf acts on them.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Limit ECC outputs to summaries with explicit uncertainty markers.
Use a checklist for any commit or shell action derived from another agent.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles security findings, session data, and hooks, while Windsurf handles workspace files and may send content to a model proxy. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty must escalate, medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared workspace files, retention and residency obligations may be triggered.
IF Windsurf's model proxy stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files.
Review vendor retention and residency settings before use.
Use redacted copies for cross-agent work.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
